道: dào — way, path, road; the Way. As a verb: to speak of, to put into words.
可: kě — can, may; admits of being ——ed (what follows it reads passively)
非: fēi — is not (negates a noun predicate; Classical Chinese has no verb 'to be')
常: cháng — constant, abiding, always-so. The Mawangdui manuscripts read 恆 héng here.
名: míng — name, reputation. As a verb: to name, to call.
無: wú — to lack, be without; nothing, non-being
之: zhī — (1) genitive particle: 'of', ''s'; (2) object pronoun: him, her, it, them; (3) rarely, a full verb: to go to, to head for (動之死地 'they stir and go to the ground of death')
有: yǒu — to have; there is; being, what-is
故: gù — (1) therefore, and so (opens a consequence); (2) as a noun, a reason, a cause — 何故 'what is the reason?'
以: yǐ — by means of it, thereby; (so as) to
其: qí — its, his, her, their (possessive pronoun)
妙: miào — subtle, wondrous; the subtlety hidden in a thing
徼: jiào — boundary, outer limit — the edge at which a thing shows itself. Wang Bi glosses it 歸終 'where things return and end'. Also read jiǎo.
者: zhě — the one(s) that — turns what precedes into a noun
同: tóng — same, alike; together, in common
出: chū — to come out, emerge, issue forth
而: ér — and yet, but; and then (links clauses)
謂: wèi — to call, to say of, to name
玄: xuán — dark — the blue-black of deep water; mysterious, unfathomable
又: yòu — again, once more; and further
眾: zhòng — the many, a multitude of
天地: tiān dì — heaven and earth; the cosmos taken as a pair
萬物: wàn wù — the ten thousand things — everything there is
兩者: liǎng zhě — the two of them, this pair
一: yī — one; the One, the undivided (抱一 'to hold the One in both arms')
上: shàng — above, upper, highest; the topmost or supreme of a set (as a verb, to go up)
下: xià — below, under, low; the lower of a pair (opposite 高 'high'); as a verb, to go down
不: bù — not (negates verbs and adjectives; nouns are negated by 非 fēi instead)
不如: bù rú — is not as good as, better to — (fixed comparative: X 不如 Y, 'X does not come up to Y')
且: qiě — and also, and moreover (joins two predicates); further, besides
中: zhōng — the middle, the centre, what is held within (read zhòng as a verb, 'to hit the mark')
久: jiǔ — long in duration, long-enduring, lasting (of time, not of length)
乎: hū — final particle: turns the sentence into a question, and is often the only sign that it is one
也: yě — sentence-final particle: closes a statement as a settled assertion, 'that is how it is'. Not the modern Mandarin 'also'.
亂: luàn — to fall into disorder, be thrown into confusion; disorder, unrest
事: shì — an affair, a matter, business to be handled; (as a verb) to serve
人: rén — a person, a human being; people, others (as against oneself)
仁: rén — benevolence, humane feeling toward others — the central Confucian virtue, which chapter 5 pointedly denies to heaven and earth
似: sì — to resemble, to seem, to be as if
作: zuò — to rise up, spring into being, start into action; to make, to do
使: shǐ — to cause, to make (someone do something): 使民不爭 'make the people not contend'; also to send, to employ
保: bǎo — to keep safe, hold on to, preserve
信: xìn — trustworthy, as good as one's word; good faith
傾: qīng — to lean, tilt, incline toward; to overturn — each of a pair tipping against the other
先: xiān — before, prior to, earlier; as a verb, to come first, to go in front
光: guāng — light, brightness, radiance; the glare a thing gives off
兒: ér — a child; in 嬰兒, a newborn
兮: xī — poetic exclamatory particle: marks a pause and lifts the line ('oh, how ——!'); it has no meaning to translate, only a rhythm
利: lì — to benefit, to do good to; profit, advantage; (of a blade) sharp
則: zé — then, in that case (introduces the consequence of what precedes); as a noun, a rule or standard
前: qián — in front, ahead; what comes before
功: gōng — achievement, merit, the work brought off; the credit for it
動: dòng — to move, to stir, to set in motion; movement, making a move
勤: qín — to toil, wear oneself out; hence (negated) to be used up, run dry
去: qù — to depart, to leave, to go away from — the classical sense, the reverse of modern Mandarin 'to go to'
吾: wú — I, my (first-person pronoun, used as subject and possessive; 我 wǒ serves as the object form)
和: hé — to blend, to bring into accord; harmony (read hè as a verb, 'to answer in sound, to chime with', as in 音聲相和)
咎: jiù — a fault, blame; the misfortune that a fault brings down on one
唯: wéi — only, it is precisely — (夫唯 X, 'it is just because X')
善: shàn — good, excellent, well-done; (as a verb) to be good at, to do well
四: sì — four; the four quarters, hence 'in every direction'
國: guó — a state, a domain, a ruler's realm — a walled capital and the land it holds, not a modern nation
堂: táng — the hall, the main room of a house
塵: chén — dust, the grime of the world
外: wài — outside, external; as a verb, to put outside, to set aside as no concern of one's own
多: duō — many, much; too much, excessive
天下: tiān xià — all under heaven — the whole inhabited world, and everyone in it
夫: fú — sentence-opening particle introducing a general observation ('now, as for ——'), and the demonstrative 'that, those'; read fū when it is the noun 'a grown man, a husband'
如: rú — to be like, to be the equal of, to come up to; if, as though
姓: xìng — a clan-name, a family line; in 百姓 'the hundred clans', the common people
嬰: yīng — a babe in arms, a newborn (chiefly in 嬰兒)
嬰兒: yīng ér — a newborn infant, a babe in arms — the Daodejing's image of unforced, undivided wholeness
子: zǐ — a child, a son; offspring (also the honorific 'Master', as in 老子 Lǎozǐ)
存: cún — to exist, be there, persist, survive; to keep in being
守: shǒu — to guard, to keep, to hold on to
宗: zōng — an ancestor, the founding forebear of a line; hence the source from which everything descends
宰: zǎi — to be master over, to rule and dispose of at will (originally the one who carves at a sacrifice)
富貴: fù guì — wealth and rank — a stock pair naming one condition, not two things
實: shí — solid, full, substantial, real; (as a verb) to fill up
專: zhuān — to concentrate, to gather into one, to keep undivided
尚: shàng — to esteem, exalt, single out for honour (a verb; distinct from 上 'above')
尤: yóu — blame, fault, cause for reproach; to find fault with
居: jū — to dwell, settle in, occupy — and so to take up a position or lay claim to it
屈: qū — to bend, to give way; to be used up, to give out (Wang Bi pairs it with 窮 'exhausted')
已: yǐ — (1) sentence-final particle: 'and that is all', giving finality; (2) as a verb, to stop, leave off, have done
帝: dì — Di, the Lord on High, god of the Shang kings (only later 'emperor')
幾: jī — to come near, verge on, be close to; the first faint stirring of a thing (read jǐ when it means 'how many')
弗: fú — does not ——it: a stronger 不, generally analysed as 不 with the object pronoun 之 fused in, so the object goes unsaid
弱: ruò — weak, yielding, soft; (as a causative verb) to make weak, to soften
強: qiáng — strong; used causatively, to make strong (read qiǎng when it means 'to force, to compel')
後: hòu — behind, after, later; (as a verb) to put behind, to place last
得: dé — to get, to obtain, to come by (難得 'hard to come by')
德: dé — potency — the power a thing has by simply being what it is; commonly rendered 'virtue'
心: xīn — the heart-mind — thinking and feeling in one organ, never merely emotion; in this book the seat of scheming and craving
志: zhì — the will, the purpose the mind is set on; ambition
恃: shì — to lean on, to presume upon — here, to claim what one has done as one's own
惡: è — ugly, ill-favoured, bad; read wù when it is the verb 'to loathe, to dislike' (chapter 8's 眾人之所惡, 'what the crowd dislikes')
愈: yù — the more, all the more (動而愈出 'move it, and the more comes out')
愛: ài — to love, care for, cherish; classically also to be sparing of, to grudge
成: chéng — to complete, to bring to fulfilment; to be finished, accomplished
或: huò — someone, something, some; perhaps, in some way. Not the modern Mandarin 'or'.
所: suǒ — stands before a verb and makes a noun of it, 'that which is ——ed': 所惡 'what is hated'
所以: suǒ yǐ — that by which, the means whereby (所 'that which' + 以 'by') — classically the how of a thing, not the modern Mandarin 'therefore'
抱: bào — to hold in both arms, to embrace, to keep clasped
持: chí — to hold, grasp, keep a grip on; to maintain
挫: cuò — to blunt, to take the edge off, to break down
揣: chuǎi — to sound out, gauge by feel; in chapter 9 traditionally taken in the older sense 'to hammer, beat to a point' (read chuí)
教: jiào — teaching, instruction (the noun; read jiāo for the verb 'to teach')
敢: gǎn — to dare, to venture to (auxiliary standing before the verb)
數: shuò — again and again, time after time (adverb; read shù 'a number', shǔ 'to count')
斯: sī — this, and just here — a demonstrative pointing back at what was said, 'and right there is ——'
於: yú — the all-purpose preposition, standing after its verb: at, in, to, toward, from, than
明: míng — bright, clear; clear-sighted, discerning; to make plain
易: yì — easy, what comes easily (the same character is also 'to change', as in 易經)
是: shì — this, this-here (a demonstrative). In Classical Chinese it is NOT the verb 'to be' — the language has none.
是以: shì yǐ — therefore, and so; a fixed connective; 是 'this' + 以 'by means of' fused into a conjunction that neither half gives you on its own
時: shí — the season, the fitting moment, timeliness; time
智: zhì — clever, knowing; cleverness — shrewd calculation, not wisdom in the good sense
柔: róu — soft, supple, pliant — the yielding quality of the newborn and of water
根: gēn — root, the root a thing grows from
梲: ruì (as read here; the graph's own reading is zhuō) — written 梲 'a short roof-post' but standing for 銳 ruì, 'to sharpen to a point'
橐: tuó — a leather bag, a sack — the bag half of a bellows
橐籥: tuó yuè — a smith's bellows: the leather bag (橐) and its blast-tube (籥) — empty within, and never out of wind
正: zhèng — upright, straight, correct; setting straight, governing (some editions print 政 zhèng 'government' here)
民: mín — the people, the common folk — the ruled, as against their ruler
氣: qì — breath, vapour, vital energy — the animating stuff of the body and of the world
沖: chōng — empty, hollow (standing for 盅 chōng, an empty vessel; Wang Bi glosses it 虛 'void'); hence also to well up, to pour forth
治: zhì — to govern, to bring into order; good order, well-ruled (the verb also used as a noun)
淵: yuān — a deep pool, a still abyss of water; unfathomably deep
湛: zhàn — deep and still, clear as unmoving water
滌: dí — to wash clean, rinse away, scour
滿: mǎn — to fill, to fill up; full to the brim
為: wéi — to do, act, make; to serve as, count as, be taken for. Read wèi when it means 'for the sake of, on account of'.
焉: yān — two jobs, and only position tells them apart: (1) the fused 於之 'in it, at it, than that', a real pronoun-plus-preposition; (2) a sentence-final particle carrying nothing but rhythm and finality. Chapter 15 has the second, chapter 17 the first.
無為: wú wéi — acting without forcing — doing that adds no contrivance or strain against the grain of things; not idleness
營: yíng — to encamp, to keep house; in 營魄, what keeps house in a body (Wang Bi's reading)
營魄: yíng pò — the bodily soul in its lodging: 營 the camp it settles in + 魄 the earthbound soul; traditionally the soul-and-body pair the sage holds together
爭: zhēng — to contend, to fight for place, to compete for
牝: pìn — the female of an animal, the dam that bears young; the female principle (its counterpart is 牡 mǔ, the male)
猶: yóu — to be like, resemble ('is it not like ——?'); also still, yet
玉: yù — jade, the most prized of stones
生: shēng — to be born, come to life; to give birth to, bring forth; life, the living
用: yòng — to use, to draw on, to put to use; use, function
畜: xù — to rear, feed, nourish, raise up (read chù as a noun: a domestic animal)
疵: cī — a flaw, a blemish — the speck in a piece of otherwise perfect jade
百: bǎi — a hundred; by extension, the whole lot of them
百姓: bǎi xìng — the hundred clans — the common people, the populace
皆: jiē — all, every one of them (an adverb: it stands before the verb, not before the noun)
盈: yíng — to be full, filled to the brim; to fill up, overflow
盜: dào — a thief, a robber; to steal
相: xiāng — one another, mutually — placed before a verb: 'X and Y —— each other' (read xiàng as a noun: an aspect, an appearance; a chief minister)
眾人: zhòng rén — the multitude, the common run of people, everybody else
知: zhī — to know, be aware of, understand; knowledge, cleverness
短: duǎn — short, of small length; shortness
神: shén — spirit, the numinous; a god; the animating spirit within a thing
私: sī — private, one's own; self-interest, what one keeps for oneself
窮: qióng — to come to an end, be exhausted, reach one's limit; brought to extremity
籥: yuè — a tube, a pipe (elsewhere a flute) — the nozzle half of a bellows
紛: fēn — a tangle, a snarl, confusion; disordered profusion
緜: mián — silk floss; a thread drawn out fine and unbroken (usually written 綿 today; doubled 緜緜, 'on and on without a break')
緜緜: mián mián — unbroken and thread-thin — a doubled descriptive of something drawn out so faintly you doubt it is there
美: měi — beautiful, fine; the beautiful (the adjective standing as a noun)
聖: shèng — sagely, wise past ordinary measure — the ideal ruler-sage of the philosophers, not 'holy'
聖人: shèng rén — the sage — in this book the ruler who holds the Way, not a moral saint
聲: shēng — sound, voice, raw noise (paired with 音 yīn, the formed musical tone)
能: néng — to be able to, can; (as a noun) capability, being equal to the thing
自: zì — self, oneself; of itself, from oneself — the reflexive always stands before its verb (自然 'so of itself')
致: zhì — to bring about, carry through to the utmost; to arrive at, attain
與: yǔ — to give; to keep company with, to deal with; with (read yù 'to take part in'; also a final particle, yú)
芻狗: chú gǒu — straw dogs — effigies plaited for a sacrifice, honoured through the rite and thrown out after
若: ruò — to be like, to resemble; if, supposing
莫: mò — no one, nothing — a negative carrying its own subject: 莫之能守 'none can keep them'
處: chǔ — to dwell in, take one's place in, occupy oneself with (read chù as a noun: a place)
虛: xū — empty, hollow, void; used causatively, to empty out
行: xíng — to walk, to go; to put into practice, carry out (read háng for 'a row, a rank')
見: jiàn — to see, to look upon; read xiàn (the causative) for 'to show, to display, to make appear'
覽: lǎn — to look over, survey, take in at a glance; the mind's inward viewing (other witnesses read 鑒 jiàn, 'mirror')
解: jiě — to untie, to loosen, to unravel (a knot or a tangle)
言: yán — to speak; words, speech, a saying
谷: gǔ — a valley, a ravine — the empty low place into which everything flows
象: xiàng — an image, a likeness; as a verb, to resemble, to look like
貨: huò — goods, commodities, valuables — things worth having and hoarding
貴: guì — costly, high in rank, honoured; as a verb, to prize, to treat as precious
賢: xián — worthy, of proven ability; a man of talent singled out for office
身: shēn — the body; hence one's own person, oneself
較: jiào — to compare, to measure one against the other (other witnesses print 形 xíng, 'give each other shape')
載: zài — to bear, to carry (Wang Bi glosses it 處 'to dwell in'; some take it as a bare opening particle. Read zǎi for 'a year, to record')
辭: cí — to decline, refuse, beg off; to take leave of; also words, a set formula of speech
退: tuì — to withdraw, to step back, to retire from the scene
遂: suì — to be carried through to completion, to succeed; thereupon
達: dá — to reach through, to get all the way, to penetrate everywhere
遺: yí — to leave behind, let drop, bequeath (read wèi when it means 'to present, to bestow')
邪: yé — final particle making a rhetorical question, 'is it not?' (read xié when it means 'crooked, perverse')
銳: ruì — sharp, keen; sharpness, a cutting point
長: cháng — long; long-lasting, for a long time. Read zhǎng when it is the verb 'to grow, to raise up' or 'to be senior over' (chapter 10's 長而不宰).
開: kāi — to open, to swing open
間: jiān — the space between, the interval (read jiàn for 'a gap; to come between, to separate')
闔: hé — to shut, to close; a door-leaf (開闔 'opening and shutting')
除: chú — to clear away, sweep out, be rid of
隨: suí — to follow, to come after (前後相隨 'front and back follow one another')
雌: cí — the hen-bird, the female; the female role — receptive, yielding (its counterpart is 雄 xióng, the male)
離: lí — to part, to come away, to be separated from
難: nán — difficult, hard to do (read nàn as a noun: a calamity, a disaster)
音: yīn — a note, a tone — the shaped, musical sound, as against 聲 the bare noise
驕: jiāo — arrogant, puffed up, overbearing — first said of a high-spirited horse
高: gāo — high, tall; lofty in station
魄: pò — the earthbound soul, the pò — the part of a person that stays with the body, as against 魂 hún, which rises
玄牝: xuán pìn — the dark female; the Daodejing's own coinage (ch. 6), the generative dark that bears endlessly without being used up
三十: sān shí — thirty (numeral; 三 'three' + 十 'ten', counted as in English)
三者: sān zhě — these three, the three of them (三 'three' + 者, which turns what precedes into a noun)
並: bìng — together, all at once, side by side (adverb before the verb: 萬物並作 'the ten thousand things all rise together'). Also written 竝.
乃: nǎi — then, and thereupon; and so it follows that — links one step of a chain to the next (容乃公，公乃全 'roomy, then even-handed; even-handed, then whole')
五: wǔ — five; the canonical set of five (five colours, five tones, five flavours — the whole range of a sense, not a mere count)
享: xiǎng — to partake of a sacrificial feast, to enjoy the offerings set out
仁義: rén yì — benevolence and rightness — the paired Confucian virtues, named together as a slogan for taught morality
今: jīn — now, the present day; what is at hand (paired against 古 gǔ, antiquity)
令: lìng — to cause, to make (someone do something); a causative verb taking a whole clause after it: 五色令人目盲 'the five colours make a man's eyes blind'. As a noun, an order.
何: hé — what? why? how? — the interrogative stands before its verb as object (吾有何患 'what trouble have I?')
侮: wǔ — to despise, to treat with contempt, to hold cheap (verb)
俗: sú — common custom, the usage of the crowd; hence commonplace, of the ordinary run
俗人: sú rén — ordinary people, the common run of men — 俗 'custom, the usual' + 人 'person'; those who live by what is customary
倍: bèi — a fold, a multiple, times over (百倍 'a hundredfold')
偽: wěi — artifice, contrivance, the made-up — what is manufactured rather than so of itself; hence falseness (noun or adjective)
儼: yǎn — grave and composed, standing on one's dignity — the bearing of a guest at a formal reception
儽: léi — worn out, listless, drooping (bound: doubled as 儽儽 in ch. 20; other editions print 儡儡 or 纍纍)
儽儽: lěi lěi — worn out and drifting, drooping with weariness — a doubled descriptive of one who has nowhere to be going
兆: zhào — an omen, the first faint sign — originally the cracks read in a scorched oracle bone; as a verb, to show a sign
全: quán — whole, entire, with nothing broken off; to keep whole, to preserve intact
公: gōng — impartial, belonging to all alike (the opposite of 私 sī 'private'); as a noun, a duke
六親: liù qīn — the six kinships — the six degrees of family bond (father, son, elder and younger brother, husband, wife), i.e. the family as an institution
共: gòng — to share, to hold in common; to come together on one thing (三十輻共一轂 'thirty spokes share one hub')
凶: xiōng — ill-omened, disastrous; calamity (adjective or noun — the opposite of 吉 jí 'auspicious')
及: jí — to reach, to come as far as; hence 'when it comes to, once' at the head of a clause
取: qǔ — to take, to take up, to take hold of; to choose one over another
古: gǔ — of old, ancient; antiquity, the earliest time (paired against 今 jīn, now)
各: gè — each one separately, every one for itself (distributive adverb standing before the verb)
味: wèi — taste, flavour; a savour on the tongue
命: mìng — what is decreed and allotted — a mandate, a destiny, and so a life-span; as a verb, to command
哉: zāi — final particle of exclamation or rhetorical question — it makes the sentence an outcry, not a statement
器: qì — a vessel, an implement — anything shaped so as to be used (noun)
國家: guó jiā — the realm and the ruling house — 國 the domain governed, 家 the noble household that governs it; together, the state
埏: shān — to knead and work (clay) with water (verb; the character is rare and is also read yán 'a border')
埴: zhí — potter's clay, the fine sticky earth worked on the wheel
執: zhí — to grasp, to hold fast to, to keep hold of (verb)
士: shì — a man of standing — the knight-officer class, hence one who has a calling and is good at it
大: dà — great, large; as an adverb, greatly. (In old texts sometimes written where 太 tài 'supreme' is meant.)
太: tài — greatest, supreme, the very highest (太上 'the highest of all')
太牢: tài láo — the Great Sacrifice — the full offering of ox, sheep and pig; hence a banquet of the highest order
央: yāng — an end, a limit, a stopping point (未央 'has not yet come to an end')
失: shī — to lose, to let slip, to be deprived of (verb; the opposite of 得 dé 'to get')
夷: yí — level, smooth, featureless — with nothing raised for the eye to catch; here the name given to what cannot be seen. (Also 'to level, raze', and the name of the eastern peoples.)
妄: wàng — reckless, without warrant, at random — acting on no ground at all (adverb or adjective)
妨: fáng — to hinder, to get in the way of, to trip up; harm done to a course of action
孝: xiào — filial devotion, the duty a child owes a parent (noun)
孩: hái — an infant, a babe in arms; as a verb, to laugh as a babe does (未孩 'not yet able to smile') and to make an infant of someone (孩之 'he babes them')
孰: shú — who? which one of them? (interrogative pronoun, standing at the head of its clause)
學: xué — to learn; learning — the book-study that fills a man with distinctions
安: ān — at rest, settled, at peace; as a verb, to bring to rest. (As an interrogative elsewhere, 'how?')
室: shì — a room, a chamber; the dwelling made by walling a space in
家: jiā — a household, a family with its estate; paired with 國 guó it makes 國家 'realm and household', the whole social order
容: róng — to hold, to contain, to make room for — hence roomy, all-embracing (ch. 16 知常容); also outward form, a look, a likeness (ch. 15 強為之容 'to force a description of it'; at 若容 some witnesses read 客 kè, 'a guest')
寄: jì — to entrust to someone's keeping, to lodge a thing with another (verb)
察: chá — to examine minutely, to look into closely; sharp-eyed, quick to tell things apart
察察: chá chá — sharply discriminating, picking everything apart — reduplication of 察 chá 'to scrutinise', so: forever inspecting
寡: guǎ — few, scant; as a verb, to make few, to cut down
寵: chǒng — favour shown by a superior, being made a favourite; as a verb, to favour
將: jiāng — about to, on the point of (an adverb before the verb: 冰之將釋 'ice about to melt'). Read jiàng for 'a general, to command'.
少: shǎo — few, little; as a verb, to make few, to reduce. (Read shào it means 'young' instead.)
屬: zhǔ — to attach to, to be joined to, to belong with (read shǔ as a noun: a class, a kind)
巧: qiǎo — skill of hand, ingenuity, artful cleverness — the craftsman's knack, taken here as contrivance
希: xī — so rare as to be barely there — of a sound, too faint to be heard (adjective; the same word as 稀 xī 'sparse')
幾何: jǐ hé — how much? how far? — literally 'how many' + 'what', an interrogative pair
廢: fèi — to fall into disuse, to be discarded, to be let go to ruin (verb, here with no agent: 大道廢 'the great Way was abandoned')
彼: bǐ — that, that other one, yonder — always set against 此 cǐ, 'this'
御: yù — to drive a chariot, to hold the reins; hence to manage, to keep in hand
復: fù — to return, to go back to where one came from; also 'again, once more' before a verb. Not the modern 'to recover'.
微: wēi — too fine to lay hold of: minute, faint, imperceptible; here the name given to what cannot be grasped
忠: zhōng — loyal, wholly given to one's lord; loyalty (adjective or noun)
恍: huǎng — dim, indistinct — glimmering at the edge of sight and gone again
悠: yōu — far off and unhurried, taking its time — of a manner, leisurely and remote (adjective)
患: huàn — trouble, calamity, affliction; as a verb, to be afflicted with, to suffer
悶: mèn — shut in, dull, undiscriminating — mind closed and unsorting (adjective; doubled as 悶悶 in ch. 20)
悶悶: mèn mèn — shut-in and unshining, giving nothing away — a doubled descriptive of one who looks dull and asks nothing
惚: hū — blurred, not to be made out (bound; pairs with 恍 huǎng as 惚恍 'indistinct')
惚恍: hū huǎng — the blur — neither seen nor unseen, a shape that will not hold still (惚 'indistinct' + 恍 'dim')
愚: yú — stupid, simple, unknowing — in the Daodejing a compliment, the mind that has not been sharpened
愚人: yú rén — the simpleton, the dullard — one who makes none of the fine distinctions the clever make
慈: cí — the tenderness of a parent for a child; motherly love (noun; the answering term to 孝 xiào)
慧: huì — quick wit, brightness of mind, cleverness
憂: yōu — worry, grief, anxious care (noun or verb)
戶: hù — a door, a single-leaf doorway (noun; smaller than 門 mén, the double gate)
搏: bó — to seize with the hand, to grapple with, to grasp at
敦: dūn — thick and solid, unworked, plain-hearted (adjective; also read duì, a ritual vessel)
文: wén — pattern, ornament, refined outward form — the figured surface of a culture, as against its plain substance
昏: hūn — dusk, failing light; hence benighted, muddled, in the dark (doubled 昏昏, dim and dull)
昏昏: hūn hūn — dim, in the dusk, muddled — reduplication of 昏 hūn 'nightfall, dark'
昧: mèi — dark, dim, hard to make out (adjective)
昭: zhāo — bright, shining out, plain for all to see (doubled 昭昭, all lit up)
昭昭: zhāo zhāo — bright, glaringly clear — reduplication of 昭 zhāo 'brilliant, manifest'
智慧: zhì huì — cleverness and quick wit — the calculating shrewdness of the clever man, not wisdom in the good sense
曠: kuàng — wide and empty, open as unbuilt country (adjective)
曰: yuē — to say; hence 'is called' — it introduces the name or the word given to a thing (歸根曰靜 'returning to the root is called stillness')
未: wèi — not yet (negates a verb for what has not happened so far; unlike 不 bù it leaves the thing still to come)
棄: qì — to throw away, to cast off, to be done with
極: jí — the utmost point, the far limit — properly the ridgepole at a roof's peak; as a verb, to reach the limit
樸: pǔ — the uncarved block — timber as it left the tree, before any tool shaped it (this one IS the standard English rendering, and we keep it)
次: cì — the next in order, the one after — 其次 'the grade below that' (noun)
止: zhǐ — to stop, to come to rest; a stopping-place, somewhere to halt
歸: guī — to go back where one belongs, to return home; of a bride, to go to her husband's house (verb)
殆: dài — danger, peril; to come to harm, to be brought into danger
沌: dùn — undivided, run together, without distinct parts (bound; doubled as 沌沌, and in 混沌 hùn dùn 'primal chaos')
沌沌: dùn dùn — all run together, nothing sorted out — a doubled descriptive of the undivided muddle (cf. 混沌, primal chaos)
沒: mò — to sink under, to be swallowed up; hence 'to the end of' — 沒身 'to the end of one's days'. Not the modern negative méi.
泊: bó — to lie moored, at anchor; hence still, unstirred, showing no ripple (read pō as a noun: a lake)
涉: shè — to ford, to wade across a stream on foot
混: hùn — to run together, to blend into one; turbid, undivided
清: qīng — clear and unclouded, as settled water; as a verb, to become clear (opposite of 濁 zhuó 'muddy')
渙: huàn — melting apart, loosening, dispersing — the way ice goes when the thaw takes it
澹: dàn — still and wide, placid as open water (adjective; also read tán)
濁: zhuó — muddy, roiled, thick with silt (the opposite of 清 qīng, clear)
然: rán — so, thus, being-so. Attached to a word it makes '——ly, in that manner'; it is the 然 of 自然 'so of itself'.
熙: xī — bright and merry, in high good humour (doubled 熙熙, all agog with pleasure)
熙熙: xī xī — merry and abustle, all in high spirits — reduplication of 熙 xī 'bright, glad'
爽: shuǎng — to go wrong, to lose its true working — of the palate, to be deadened and taste nothing rightly. Not the modern Mandarin 'refreshing'.
牢: láo — the pen for sacrificial beasts, hence the victims themselves and the feast made of them (太牢, the full ox-sheep-pig offering)
狀: zhuàng — shape, the look a thing has, visible form (noun)
狂: kuáng — mad, wild, out of one's senses
獨: dú — alone, by oneself, and no one else — 我獨 'I alone' (adverb or adjective)
獵: liè — to hunt, to chase game
畋: tián — to hunt, to drive game in the field (verb)
畋獵: tián liè — the great hunt — 畋 beating the fields for game and 獵 running it down
畏: wèi — to fear, to stand in awe of (verb; 所畏 'what people fear')
當: dāng — to face, to be right at — 'just there where' (當其無 'right there where it is empty'). Read dàng for 'fitting, to match'.
登: dēng — to climb, to mount up onto (verb)
發: fā — to shoot, to let fly (an arrow from the bow); hence to break out into, to burst forth in
皦: jiǎo — dazzling white, glaringly bright (adjective; a rare character)
盜賊: dào zéi — thieves and brigands — 盜 the one who takes by stealth, 賊 the one who takes by force
篤: dǔ — solid, unwavering, held to in earnest (adjective or adverb)
紀: jì — the main cord of a skein or net, the thread that holds the rest in order; hence the guiding line, the ordering principle
素: sù — undyed silk, plain white — the unbleached, unstained thing before any pattern is put on it (the cloth answering to 樸 'the uncarved block' in wood)
絕: jué — to cut off, to sever clean, to have done with entirely
繩: shéng — a cord, a rope; a plumb-line, hence a standard. Doubled as 繩繩 it means 'on and on, unbroken like a cord'.
繩繩: shéng shéng — on and on unbroken, cord upon cord — a doubled descriptive of what runs endlessly and cannot be told apart (繩 a rope)
義: yì — rightness, what duty requires of one (noun; the Confucian virtue paired with 仁 rén)
聞: wén — to hear, to catch a sound (the result; 聽 tīng is the listening that may or may not achieve it)
聽: tīng — to listen, to give ear to (as against 聞 wén, to hear what reaches you)
聾: lóng — deaf; as a verb, to make deaf (adjective or verb)
臣: chén — a subject, a servant of the ruler; a minister of state
自然: zì rán — so of itself — what is as it is of its own accord, with nothing making it so (自 'self' + 然 'so')
臺: tái — a raised terrace, a look-out platform built up to be climbed
色: sè — colour; the look or appearance of a thing (noun)
芸: yún — a fragrant herb; growing thick and rank (doubled 芸芸, in teeming profusion)
芸芸: yún yún — teeming, thick and rank as growing grass — reduplication of 芸 yún, a fragrant herb, to flourish
若何: ruò hé — how so? by how much? — literally 'like what?'
荒: huāng — waste and uncleared, wild; hence boundless, running out beyond sight (adjective)
蔽: bì — to cover over, to keep screened from view (some witnesses print 敝 bì, 'worn, shabby'): 蔽不新成, to stay covered rather than newly made up
視: shì — to look at, to turn the eyes on (the looking; 見 jiàn is the seeing that results)
親: qīn — kin, blood relations (六親, the six degrees of kindred); as a verb, to draw close to, to hold dear
託: tuō — to commit to another's charge, to entrust (verb; near-synonym of 寄 jì)
詰: jié — to question closely, to press with inquiry, to run a thing to the bottom
識: shí — to know, to recognise for what it is; knowledge. (Read zhì it means 'to record, a mark' instead.)
譽: yù — to praise, to speak well of; praise, good repute
豫: yù — wary, hanging back — the beast that keeps stopping to check; hence hesitant, on guard. Not the modern 'pleased'.
賊: zéi — a robber who takes by violence; as a verb, to injure, to do harm to
足: zú — enough, sufficient; as a verb, to suffice. Also the foot.
輻: fú — the spoke of a wheel (noun)
轂: gǔ — the nave of a wheel — the hub the spokes run into, hollow at the centre for the axle
辱: rǔ — disgrace, being put to shame; as a verb, to humiliate (the answering term to 寵 chǒng 'favour')
迎: yíng — to go out to meet, to face what is coming toward you (paired with 隨 suí, to follow behind)
通: tōng — to pass right through without obstruction, to get through; unobstructed, open (verb or adjective)
道紀: dào jì — the thread of the Way — the guiding cord (紀) running through it, by which the whole is held in order
鄙: bǐ — of the outlying villages, hence boorish, coarse, unpolished (adjective; as a noun, a border hamlet)
鄰: lín — a neighbour, the households next to one's own (四鄰, the neighbours on all four sides)
釋: shì — to let go, to loosen, to melt away — of ice, to thaw (verb)
鑿: záo — to chisel out, to cut a hole through
阿: ē — a slow, grudging 'yeah' — the careless answer set against 唯 wěi, the prompt respectful 'yes'. (Elsewhere: to fawn on, to curry favour; a river-bend.)
靜: jìng — still, at rest, unmoving; as a verb, to bring to stillness, to let settle
頑: wán — blockish, dull as unworked stone; stubborn (adjective)
飂: liáo — the high wind blowing far off; blown along, adrift and not settling
食: shí — to eat, to feed on; food. (Read sì it means 'to feed another' — 食母 in ch. 20 is read either way: 'to feed from the mother' or 'the nursing mother'.)
餘: yú — surplus, what is left over, more than enough
首: shǒu — the head; hence the front, the first, the beginning (noun; answered by 後 hòu 'the rear')
馳: chí — to gallop, to drive a horse hard
馳騁: chí chěng — to gallop hard, to course about on horseback — 馳 and 騁 both mean 'to gallop', doubled up for speed
騁: chěng — to give a horse its head, to race unchecked over open country
驚: jīng — to be startled, to take fright — of a horse, to shy; as a noun, a shock
五色: wǔ sè — the five colours (blue-green, red, yellow, white, black); a fixed set-term for the whole visible palette, not a count
五音: wǔ yīn — the five tones of the pentatonic scale; a fixed set-term for music as such
五味: wǔ wèi — the five flavours (sour, bitter, sweet, pungent, salty); a fixed set-term for taste as such
太上: tài shàng — the highest of all; a fixed term for the best kind of ruler, not simply 'very high'
主: zhǔ — the lord, the one in charge — the ruler of a state, the master of a house (noun; as a verb, to preside over)
乘: shèng — a war-chariot and its team of four horses; the counting-word for chariots, by which a state's size was reckoned (萬乘 'ten thousand chariots'). Read chéng for the verb 'to mount, to ride'.
亦: yì — also, likewise, equally so (adverb, standing before the verb)
人主: rén zhǔ — the lord of men, the sovereign (人 'people' + 主 'master') — the ruler as the one the people are under
企: qǐ — to stand up on tiptoe, to crane oneself higher (verb; the strained posture nobody can hold)
伐: fá — to blow one's own trumpet, to make a show of what one has done (自伐 'to praise oneself'); properly to hew or strike, hence to press a claim
佐: zuǒ — to assist, to second, to serve as counsellor to (verb)
兵: bīng — a weapon, arms; hence soldiers, armed force, war. Classically the blade first, the man carrying it second.
冥: míng — dark, unlit — too deep in shadow to make anything out (adjective)
凶年: xiōng nián — a year of dearth, a famine year (凶 'ill-omened, calamitous' + 年 'harvest') — the crop failure that follows an army
制: zhì — properly to cut out cloth, to tailor; hence to shape, to regulate, to govern, and the ordering so made (大制, the great ordering)
割: gē — to cut apart, to carve up, to sever a piece off (大制不割 'the great shaping does not cut')
勿: wù — do not (prohibitive: forbids an action, where 不 bù merely denies one)
反: fǎn — to turn back, to go the reverse way, to come round again — the Way's own motion, not mere opposition (later written 返)
君: jūn — a lord, a prince — the one who rules over something (noun)
吹: chuī — to blow hard, to puff out (paired here with 歔 xū, the slow warm breath — one breath cools, the other warms)
周: zhōu — to go all the way round, to reach everywhere; complete on every side (周行, to circle without leaving a gap)
在: zài — to be in, to lie in, to be present at; of a thing's standing, to consist in (其在道也 'as it stands in respect of the Way')
域: yù — a bounded territory, the space inside its borders (域中, within the bounds — all the room there is)
壯: zhuàng — at full strength, grown stout and vigorous, in its prime — the state just before decline
奈: nài — to cope with, to do anything about (occurs only in 奈何, 'what is to be done about —?')
奈何: nài hé — how can it be that…?, what is to be done about…? (fixed interrogative: 奈 'to cope with' + 何 'what'), here voiced as indignation
奢: shē — extravagance, lavishness, going well past what is needed (noun/adjective)
好: hào — to be given to, to be apt to — before a verb, 'readily does' (其事好還 'that business readily comes back on you'). Read hǎo for 'good, fine'.
孔: kǒng — a hole, an opening; hence vast, all-embracing. Wang Bi glosses it 空 'empty' — 孔德, the potency that is hollow.
字: zì — to give a style-name to, to style (verb). The 字 is the courtesy-name conferred on a man besides his given 名 — so 字之曰道 is a title of address, not the thing's real name.
官: guān — an office of state, an official post; the officer who holds it (noun)
官長: guān zhǎng — the chief of the officers, head over the functionaries (官 'an office-holder' + 長 zhǎng 'senior, chief')
寂: jì — silent, without a sound; still and unstirring (adjective)
寥: liáo — empty and soundless, boundlessly vacant — with nothing in it and nothing to be heard
師: shī — (1) a teacher, the man others take as model; (2) an army in the field (ch. 30, 師之所處, 'where the host has camped')
年: nián — a harvest, the ripening of the grain; hence a year, counted by that turn
式: shì — a model, a pattern others measure themselves by; a standard, a norm (noun)
彰: zhāng — to stand out plainly, to be conspicuous, to be made manifest (of a reputation, to be displayed)
從: cóng — to follow, to go along behind; to comply with, to take one's lead from (verb)
從事: cóng shì — to take up a practice, to go about one's business in something (從 'to follow' + 事 'affair, undertaking')
必: bì — inevitably, is bound to (adverb before the verb: what must follow)
忒: tè — to deviate, to slip from the mark, to go wrong — said of what ought to be unvarying
惑: huò — to be at a loss, led astray, no longer knowing which way to take (verb)
惟: wéi — only, none but (惟道是從 'follows the Way alone'); before a predicate it may merely mark it, adding nothing (惟恍惟惚 'now dim, now blurred')
改: gǎi — to change, to alter, to become other than it was (verb)
救: jiù — to bring help to, to rescue, to get out of trouble (救人 'to salvage people', not to reform them)
敗: bài — to spoil, to wreck, to bring to ruin (transitive); to be defeated, to come to grief (intransitive)
敝: bì — worn out, tattered, threadbare — cloth used until it falls apart
散: sàn — to break up, to be scattered apart — of the uncarved block, to be cut into pieces (verb)
日: rì — the sun; hence a day (終日 'the day through')
早: zǎo — early, soon, before its time (adverb)
曲: qū — bent, crooked, curved; to give way rather than break (the answering term to 全 quán 'whole')
朝: zhāo — a morning, the space of one morning. (Read cháo it is the ruler's court, or to attend it — not here.)
本: běn — the root and butt of a tree, its base; hence the foundation, what a thing stands on (opposite 末 mò, the twig-tips)
枉: wǎng — bent, crooked, warped out of true (adjective; the answering term to 直 zhí 'straight')
果: guǒ — fruit; hence the thing brought off, the result and no more than the result. Wang Bi glosses it 濟 jì, 'to carry through'.
棘: jí — a thorn bush, a bramble (noun)
楗: jiàn — the upright bar dropped into a gate to hold it shut (also written 鍵); the mate of 關, the crossbar
榮: róng — in flower, in full bloom; hence splendour, glory, honour (set against 辱 rǔ 'disgrace')
樂: lè — to be glad of, to take pleasure in (道亦樂得之 'the Way too is glad to get him'). Read yuè for 'music', yào for 'to be fond of'.
歔: xū — to breathe out softly, to let the breath go warm and slow (set against 吹 chuī, to blow hard and cold)
況: kuàng — how much more so — the a-fortiori word, opening the stronger case (而況於人乎 'how much more, then, with a man?')
法: fǎ — a rule, a model to go by; as a verb, to take as one's model, to pattern oneself on (人法地, man patterns himself on earth)
泰: tài — going too far, extravagance, overdoing it; properly 'grand, at one's ease', and so ease indulged past measure
燕: yàn — at ease, in quiet retirement (燕處, to dwell at rest). Properly the swallow; read yān it is the state of Yan.
王: wáng — a king, the sovereign (noun). Read wàng for the verb 'to reign as king over'.
瑕: xiá — a flaw in a piece of jade, a blemish (noun)
瑕讁: xiá zhé — flaw and fault-finding — 瑕 the blemish in a piece of jade + 讁 the thing one is reproached for; together, anything to pick at
甚: shèn — exceedingly, very (adverb); as a noun, excess — the going-too-far that is put away (ch. 29 去甚)
甫: fǔ — a beginning, a first putting-forth; Wang Bi glosses 眾甫 as 物之始 'the beginnings of things'. Elsewhere a respectful word for a man.
直: zhí — straight, true, upright; straightened out (adjective; the answering term to 枉 wǎng 'bent')
真: zhēn — genuine, not counterfeit; true to what the thing actually is (of the 精, that it is really there)
眾甫: zhòng fǔ — the beginnings of the many — all things at their first start. Wang Bi glosses 眾甫 as 物之始, 'the beginning of things'.
矜: jīn — to plume oneself, to make much of one's own worth (自矜 'to set store by oneself'); in other contexts, to pity
窈: yǎo — deep and out of sight, sunk far down in shadow (adjective)
窪: wā — a hollow, a sunken low place; hollowed out, dished (and so able to be filled)
立: lì — to stand, to stand firm, to hold one's footing; to be set up (verb)
策: cè — a bamboo slip; a counting-rod, the tally used in reckoning (also a horse-whip)
籌: chóu — a counting rod, a tally stick used in reckoning (noun)
籌策: chóu cè — counting-rods, the bamboo tallies laid out to reckon with — hence calculation itself
精: jīng — the finest essence — the concentrated vital stuff at the heart of a thing (noun; properly the cleaned, hulled grain)
約: yuē — to bind fast, to tie up; a binding, and so an agreement (繩約 'a cord's fastening')
終: zhōng — to run out to the end, to last the whole of (不終朝, does not last out a morning); the end, at last
結: jié — to tie, to knot, to fasten one thing to another
繩約: shéng yuē — cord and knot — a fastening made with rope: 繩 the cord, 約 the tying of it
羸: léi — weak, wasted, worn thin — feeble in the body (the answering term to 強 qiáng 'strong')
老: lǎo — to grow old, to pass into age and decay (verb); old, aged
荊: jīng — the thorn-bush, bramble (chiefly in 荊棘) — scrub that takes over abandoned ground
荊棘: jīng jí — briars and thorns — the scrub that overruns ground once men have left it
萬乘: wàn shèng — ten thousand chariots — the fixed measure of a great state, named by the war-chariots it could field, and so a byword for its ruler
襲: xí — to put one robe on over another, hence to keep covered, to carry hidden (襲明, a clarity worn out of sight)
襲明: xí míng — clarity kept covered — 襲 'to wear one garment over another, to cover over' + 明 'clear-sightedness': discernment that does not show itself. (襲 also means 'to inherit, to take over'.)
要: yào — the essential point, what a thing turns on (要妙, the subtlety at the heart of the matter). Read yāo it is the waist, or to demand.
要妙: yào miào — the essential subtlety — 要 'the crux, what the thing turns on' + 妙 'the subtle': the fine point on which it all hangs
誠: chéng — truly, in very fact (adverb); as a noun, being wholly what one is, without pretence
讁: zhé — to reproach, to call to account; a fault worth blaming (a variant writing of 謫)
谿: xī — a mountain stream-bed, the ravine that everything drains down into (noun; variant of 溪)
豈: qǐ — how could it possibly…? — puts a rhetorical question expecting 'no'; stands before its verb, usually with 哉 or 乎 at the close
資: zī — stock, material to work with — what a man draws upon (noun)
贅: zhuì — a wart, a lump of surplus flesh; anything stuck on that has no business being there
超: chāo — to leap over, to pass clean beyond (verb; 超然, standing above it all and apart)
超然: chāo rán — standing clear of it all, above and apart (超 'to leap over, to pass beyond' + 然, which makes it '——ly')
跨: kuà — to stride, to straddle with over-long steps (verb; the stride that cannot be kept up)
躁: zào — restless, fidgety, unable to keep still — hurried motion (the answering term to 靜 jìng 'still')
軍: jūn — an army, a host in the field (noun; properly the encamped host)
輕: qīng — light in weight; hence slight, of no account. As a verb, to make light of, to treat as weighing nothing.
輜: zī — a covered baggage waggon, the supply cart of an army (noun)
輜重: zī zhòng — the baggage-train — 輜 the covered supply-wagon + 重 the heavy gear; an army's stores, which the commander never marches away from
轍: zhé — the rut a wheel cuts in the road (noun)
轍迹: chè jì — ruts and footprints — 轍 the track a cartwheel cuts + 迹 the mark of a foot; the traces that show someone has passed
迷: mí — to lose the way, to be led astray; deluded, gone wrong (verb/adjective)
迹: jì — a footprint, a track, the trace left behind by passing
逝: shì — to go away, to pass on and keep going — departing without return (verb)
遠: yuǎn — far off, distant; to go far away. Read yuàn for the verb 'to keep at a distance'.
還: huán — to come back round, to return upon its own starting point (verb; here, what is done comes back on the doer). Read hái it is the adverb 'still'.
重: zhòng — heavy, weighty; hence grave, of consequence; as a verb, to treat as weighty. Read chóng for 'again, doubled'.
閉: bì — to shut, to close up a door (verb)
閱: yuè — to pass in review, to inspect them one by one as they file past — properly the mustering of troops at the gate (門)
關: guān — the bar across a gate, the bolt that fastens it (noun; as a verb, to bar, to shut)
關楗: guān jiàn — bar and bolt — 關 the crossbar drawn across a gate + 楗 the upright pin that holds it; the whole fastening of a door
隳: huī — to pull down, to wreck, to be brought to ruin (verb)
雄: xióng — the cock-bird, the male; the male part — assertive, forward (its counterpart is 雌 cí, the hen)
雖: suī — although, even though (conjunction opening the concessive clause)
雨: yǔ — rain. Read yù for the verb 'to rain, to rain down'.
飄: piāo — to whirl, to be tossed about on the wind; of wind, to gust (飄風 'a squall, a sudden gale')
驟: zhòu — at a gallop, hence sudden and violent (驟雨, a cloudburst) — properly of a horse driven fast
黑: hēi — black, unlit dark — plain black, as against 玄 xuán, the blue-black of depth
神器: shén qì — the sacred vessel; a standing classical term for sovereign power, and one Wang Bi christens outright (故謂之神器也)
丈: zhàng — a measure of ten 尺, about a man's height; hence 'full-grown, of full stature' (in 丈夫 'a grown man')
丈夫: zhàng fū — a grown man, a man of full stature (丈 a ten-foot measure + 夫 a man); 大丈夫 is 'the truly great man', the one worth the name
不穀: bù gǔ — 'the Ungood One' (literally 'not-grain', not-nourishing) — one of a ruler's humble self-designations, alongside 孤 and 寡 (noun, used only of oneself)
亡: wáng — to perish, be lost, come to nothing (verb; 不亡 'does not perish'). Also read wú, borrowed for 無 'to lack'.
佳: jiā — fine, excellent, handsome (adjective; 佳兵 'fine weapons', said with irony)
侯: hóu — a feudal lord, ruler of a domain — the rank below the king (侯王, 'lords and kings', the holders of power)
侯王: hóu wáng — the lords and the king, i.e. those who hold rule (bound compound: 侯 a feudal lord + 王 a king)
偏: piān — off to one side, secondary, subordinate; hence 'deputy' (偏將軍, the second-in-command general, as against 上將軍)
利器: lì qì — sharp implement, instrument of power (bound compound: 利 sharp, advantageous + 器 vessel, tool)
前識: qián shí — foreknowledge, knowing a thing in advance (前 'before' + 識 'to know'). Wang Bi takes it as knowing before other men do.
剛: gāng — hard, rigid, unyielding (the opposite of 柔 supple)
剛強: gāng qiáng — the hard and the strong, taken as one condition — 剛 unbending like metal + 強 forceful; the standing opposite of 柔弱 'soft and yielding'
勝: shèng — to overcome, get the better of, prevail over; a victory (戰勝 'win the battle'). Read shēng it means 'to be equal to, to bear'.
化: huà — to transform, to be transformed; transformation (verb; 自化 'transform of themselves')
厚: hòu — thick, substantial, deep-laid — what has body to it (the opposite of 薄 bó 'thin, worn away')
右: yòu — the right hand, the right-hand side — in the old ritual the lesser and inauspicious side, the place of mourning and of war (noun)
合: hé — to come together, join, close upon each other (天地相合 'heaven and earth join'); to match, to fit
吉: jí — auspicious, of good omen (adjective; 吉事 'an auspicious occasion')
君子: jūn zǐ — the gentleman: a man of rank and of character (literally 'a ruler's son'), the Confucian ideal the chapter measures against
哀: āi — grief, sorrow; to grieve for, to mourn (noun or verb)
喪: sāng — mourning, funeral rites (noun; 喪禮 'the rites of mourning'). Read sàng it is the verb 'to lose, to forfeit'.
喪禮: sāng lǐ — the rites of mourning, funeral observance (bound compound: 喪 here read sāng 'mourning' — as a verb it is sàng 'to lose' — + 禮 rite)
固: gù — firm, solid, fixed fast; as an adverb, 'assuredly'. In 必固張之 it carries the sense 'first of all, for the moment' — you must first stretch a thing out.
均: jūn — even, level, equally apportioned; to come out even, to level off of itself (adjective or verb)
基: jī — the foundation, the packed base a wall is raised on; what a thing rests on
壽: shòu — long life, length of days; long-lived (noun or adjective)
大象: dà xiàng — the Great Image — the vast form the Way presents, which has no shape you could point to (大 'great' + 象 'image, figure')
奪: duó — to seize, wrest away, take by force (verb)
孤: gū — orphaned, left alone, without kin; used by a ruler of himself, 'the Orphaned One' — a title of self-abasement
定: dìng — to settle, come to rest; settled, stable (verb or adjective)
客: kè — a guest; a stranger passing through, a traveller who stops and moves on (opposite of 主 'the host, the master')
害: hài — to harm, injure; harm, injury (verb or noun)
寧: níng — settled, at rest, still — of the earth, steady under everything; to be at peace
將軍: jiāng jūn — a general, commander of an army (bound compound: 將 here read jiāng 'commander' — elsewhere jiāng 'about to' — + 軍 army)
小: xiǎo — small, slight, of no account; as a noun, 'the small' — what is beneath notice
左: zuǒ — the left hand, the left-hand side — in the old ritual the honoured and auspicious side, the place of peace (noun)
左右: zuǒ yòu — left and right, hence 'to either hand, every which way' (左 + 右); of a ruler, also his attendants
平: píng — level, even, flat; at peace, untroubled (adjective)
張: zhāng — to stretch open, draw taut, spread wide (originally of stringing and drawing a bow)
往: wǎng — to go toward, make one's way to, resort to (verb; 天下往 'all under heaven goes to it')
微明: wēi míng — the faint light — discernment so slight it is barely visible (微 'too fine to lay hold of' + 明 'clear-sightedness'); a term the text christens here, 是謂微明
忠信: zhōng xìn — loyalty and good faith, the paired Confucian virtues (bound compound: 忠 loyal + 信 trustworthy)
恐: kǒng — to fear; before a verb, 'it is to be feared that it will —', hence 'in danger of, likely to' (將恐裂 'is likely to split')
恬: tián — calm, quiet, unstirred, holding nothing dear (adjective)
悲: bēi — grief, sorrow; to mourn, to be stricken
應: yìng — to answer, respond to a call (verb; distinguish yīng 'ought to', not the sense here)
戰: zhàn — to give battle, wage war; a battle (戰勝 'to conquer in battle')
扔: rēng — to pull, drag by force, haul into line (verb; a rare word, also read réng — not the modern sense 'to throw away')
攘: rǎng — to push the sleeve back and bare the arm — the gesture of a man about to lay hands on you (攘臂); also 'to snatch, to seize'
既: jì — (1) already, by now, having done; (2) as a verb, to be used up, come to an end
昔: xī — formerly, of old, in ancient times (昔之 'those of old who…')
柔弱: róu ruò — soft and yielding, supple and weak (bound compound: 柔 supple + 弱 weak)
歇: xiē — to give out, cease, be spent — of a spirit, to die away; of an effort, to stop
歙: xī — to draw in, contract, suck shut (verb; the opposite of 張 'to spread open'; distinguish shè, a place name)
殺: shā — to kill, to put to death (殺人 'to kill men'). Read shài it means 'to reduce, to diminish'.
氾: fàn — to overflow, flood over; hence spreading everywhere, all-pervading (verb or adjective)
江: jiāng — a great river; in classical usage the Yangtze in particular, as 河 is the Yellow River (江海 'the great rivers and the sea')
泣: qì — to weep silently, shed tears without wailing; tears (verb or noun)
淡: dàn — bland, thin, without savour — said of taste and of temper alike: unseasoned, unexcited, not keen
滅: miè — to be put out, die out, be wiped away (verb, of a flame or a life)
珞: luò — only in the doubled 珞珞: hard, rough and stony, as a common rock is
珞珞: luò luò — hard and stony, rugged, common as gravel (bound reduplication of 珞; a descriptive, said of stone)
琭: lù — only in the doubled 琭琭: gleaming and rare, as jade is
琭琭: lù lù — glittering, prized, rare as fine jade (bound reduplication of 琭; a descriptive, said of jade)
甘: gān — sweet to the taste; pleasant, delicious (甘露 'sweet dew')
甘露: gān lù — sweet dew, the dew that falls when heaven and earth are in accord — an omen of good rule (bound compound: 甘 sweet + 露 dew)
矣: yǐ — sentence-final particle: marks the situation as newly reached or now settled — 'and there it is', 'that is that'
示: shì — to show, to display to someone, to let be seen (示人 'to show it to others')
祥: xiáng — auspicious, of good omen; a good omen (adjective or noun; 不祥 'ill-omened')
禮: lǐ — rite, ceremony; and beyond that the whole code of proper conduct — 'the rites', last and outermost of the virtues this chapter ranks
稱: chēng — to call, name, style; to style oneself (verb; distinguish chèn 'to fit, match')
穀: gǔ — grain, the standing corn; hence 'well-provided, good', so that 不穀 'the ungood' served a ruler as a humble self-name. A different character from 谷 gǔ 'valley'.
竭: jié — to run dry, be drained, be exhausted (verb, of a spring or a valley)
脫: tuō — to slip out of, get free of, escape from (魚不可脫於淵 'the fish cannot leave the deep')
臂: bì — the arm (noun; 攘臂 'to bare the arm', the gesture of forcing a thing through)
興: xīng — to raise up, set going, make flourish (verb). Read xìng it is the noun 'a lift of pleasure, an impulse'.
華: huá — flower, blossom; hence outward show, showiness (noun; distinguish huà, a name)
薄: bó — thin, meagre, worn down to nothing much — what is left of a thing when its substance has gone (opposite of 厚 hòu 'thick')
衣: yī — clothing, a garment (noun); as a verb, read yì, to clothe, to cover over
裂: liè — to split apart, tear open, rend (of heaven: to crack across)
譬: pì — to liken, compare; by way of comparison (verb, often opening a simile)
貞: zhēn — steadfast and upright; the fixed standard by which the rest are set straight (為天下貞, 'to be the standard for all under heaven')
賓: bīn — a guest; as a verb, to come as a guest does, to render homage of one's own accord (noun or verb)
賤: jiàn — low, base, of no rank or price — the opposite of 貴 guì 'held in honour'; as a verb, to think little of
蹶: jué — to stumble and fall, to topple over (verb; also read guì)
輿: yú — a carriage, properly the body of a cart — a thing that is nothing but its assembled parts. Some witnesses read 譽 yù 'praise' here instead.
過: guò — to pass by, go past; to exceed, overstep; a fault (verb or noun)
過客: guò kè — a passer-by, a traveller who halts on his way through and does not stay (過 'to pass by' + 客 'guest, stranger')
鎮: zhèn — to press down, weight down, hold steady (verb; the weight that keeps a thing from stirring)
降: jiàng — to send down, let fall — of heaven letting down rain or dew (以降甘露). Read xiáng it means 'to submit, to surrender'.
露: lù — dew (noun; distinguish lòu 'to expose to view')
靈: líng — numinous, charged with spirit-power; of a spirit, potent and able to answer (神得一以靈)
養: yǎng — to nourish, feed, rear, keep alive (verb)
餌: ěr — a dainty, good food set out — a cake or delicacy; and so also the bait on a hook
偷: tōu — slack, remiss, done anyhow (adjective here: 建德若偷 'potency well set up looks shirking'); the familiar sense 'to filch, steal' is the later everyday one
兕: sì — the wild ox — a one-horned beast of the southern marshes, often identified with the rhinoceros, whose hide made the best armour (noun)
入: rù — to go in, enter (verb; the standing opposite of 出 chū 'go out' — 出生入死 'come out into life, go in to death')
刃: rèn — the blade, the cutting edge of a weapon (noun; 兵 bīng is the weapon entire, 刃 the edge of it)
卻: què — to send back, turn away, push back (verb; 卻走馬 'sends the fast horses back' from the army to the fields)
堅: jiān — hard, unyielding, solid — what will not give (adjective; the answering term to 柔 róu 'soft, supple')
寒: hán — cold (noun/adjective; the cold itself, what 躁 restlessness is said to overcome)
建: jiàn — to set upright, to plant, to establish — hence firmly-founded, well-set (verb, and adjectivally: 建言 'the established sayings', 建德 'potency well planted')
建言: jiàn yán — the standing sayings, the maxims handed down (bound compound: 建 'set up, establish' + 言 'words'; 故建言有之 introduces the string of proverbs that follows, and may name a lost collection)
弊: bì — to wear out, to grow ragged with use, to give out (verb; the image is a worn garment). Also an abuse, a thing gone bad.
強梁: qiáng liáng — overbearing, a man of force (bound compound: 強 qiáng 'forceful' + 梁 'roof-beam' — one who throws his weight about; 強梁者 'the violent man')
彌: mí — the more, ever the more (adverb of rising degree, paired across two clauses: 其出彌遠，其知彌少 'the further out he goes, the less he knows'). As a verb, to fill up, to stretch clean across.
形: xíng — shape, visible form, the outline a thing shows (noun)
徒: tú — a company, a following, those who belong to one kind — 生之徒 'the company of the living'. Root sense: going on foot, hence a footman, a follower, a disciple.
戎: róng — war, arms, the military (noun/attributive; 戎馬 'war-horse' — not the tribal name here)
戎馬: róng mǎ — war-horses — the chariot teams of an army in the field; 戎 'arms, warfare' + 馬 'horse'
投: tóu — to hurl, drive in, thrust (verb; 投其角 'to drive in its horn')
拙: zhuō — clumsy, unhandy, without knack (adjective; the answering term to 巧 qiǎo 'skill of hand')
措: cuò — to lay, set down, put in place (verb; 措其爪 'to set its claws to anything')
損: sǔn — to take away from, to diminish, to pare down; a loss (verb and noun; the answering term to 益 yì 'to add to')
攝: shè — to take hold of, keep in hand, husband (verb; 攝生 'to hold one's life well in hand', to nurture it)
教父: jiào fù — the father of the teaching — the founding maxim a doctrine is fathered on, not a person; 教 'teaching' + 父 'father'
方: fāng — a square, the four-cornered (noun/adjective; 大方無隅 'the great square has no corners'). Elsewhere also 'quarter, region; method'
是故: shì gù — for this reason, therefore — a fused connective read as one word, 是 'this' + 故 'reason' (compare 是以)
晚: wǎn — late, late in coming (adverb/adjective; 大器晚成 'the great vessel is late finished')
梁: liáng — a beam, a roof-tree, a bridge (noun); in the compound 強梁 the beam's stiffness stands for the man who will not bend
歙歙: xī xī — drawn-in, self-effacing, holding no mind of his own (doubled descriptive; 歙 xī is to draw the breath in — Wang Bi glosses the pair 心無所主 'the heart has nothing it makes its master')
注: zhù — to pour, to pour into (of water); hence to pour one's attention into, to fix upon — 注其耳目 'they pour their ears and eyes into him'
渝: yú — to change, shift, lose its colour, come out sullied (verb; 質真若渝 'true substance looks like something that has run')
渾: hún — turbid, unsorted, all of one piece — water with the mud still in it; as a verb here, to leave undivided, to let no distinctions settle out. Also read hùn 'to mix, to confound'.
熱: rè — heat, the hot (noun/adjective; paired against 寒 hán 'cold')
父: fù — father (noun; 教父 'the father of the teaching', the principle everything else is born from). Read fǔ only as an honorific for an old man
王公: wáng gōng — kings and dukes — the ruling nobility taken together; 王 'king' + 公 'duke, lord'
甲: jiǎ — armour, a coat of mail (noun; 甲兵 'armour and weapons', i.e. arming for war)
病: bìng — sickness, an ailment; hence harm, the thing that does damage — 孰病 'which of them is the affliction?'. As a verb, to be a trouble, to suffer from.
益: yì — to increase, add to; gain, benefit (verb and noun; 為學日益 'in study you add daily', 無為之益 'the gain of acting without forcing')
禍: huò — calamity, ruin, the disaster that comes down on a man (noun; the answering term to 福 fú 'good fortune')
笑: xiào — to laugh; to laugh at (verb; 大笑之 'laughs aloud at it')
糞: fèn — dung, manure; as a verb, to dung the fields, to manure the land
纇: lèi — a knot or snarl in silk thread, hence rough, uneven, snagged (noun/adjective; rare character — 夷道若纇 'the level way looks knotted')
缺: quē — chipped, broken at the rim — a jar with a piece gone; hence wanting, incomplete (adjective)
至: zhì — to reach, arrive at (verb: 以至於無為 'arriving at acting without forcing'); before an adjective, 'utmost, most' (至柔 'the utmost soft')
蓋: gài — sentence-opening particle: 'as one hears it', 'presumably' — flags what follows as taken on report rather than asserted. Root sense: a thatched cover, a lid; hence to cover over.
藏: cáng — to store up, hoard, keep back (verb; 多藏 'hoarding much'). Read zàng only as a noun, 'a storehouse, a treasury'
被: pī — to put on, wear (armour) (verb; 不被甲兵 'puts on no armour and weapons'). The reading bèi, which marks the passive, is the other word and is not what stands here
角: jiǎo — a horn, an animal's horn (noun). Read jué for 'to contend, to match oneself against'.
訥: nè — slow of speech, halting, tongue-tied (adjective; 大辯若訥 'the great argument sounds tongue-tied')
負: fù — to carry on the back, to bear behind one — paired here with 抱 bào 'to clasp in front'. Also to shoulder a burden, to owe, to be worsted.
貸: dài — to lend out, grant, bestow (verb; 善貸且成 'good at bestowing, and at bringing to completion')
費: fèi — outlay, expense, what is spent (noun); as a verb, to use up, to squander
質: zhì — substance, the solid inner stuff of a thing (noun; the classical counterpart to 文 wén, outward polish)
走: zǒu — to run, to go at speed — the classical sense; the modern Mandarin 'to walk' is later. 走馬 are the fast horses, the racers.
走馬: zǒu mǎ — running horses, chargers (bound compound; 走 in classical Chinese is 'to run', not modern 'to walk', so these are horses at the gallop — war-horses stood down to cart dung)
辯: biàn — argument, pleading, eloquence; to argue a case (noun/verb)
進: jìn — to advance, to press forward, to go on (verb; the answering term to 退 tuì 'to withdraw')
遇: yù — to meet with, run into, come up against (verb; 不遇兕虎 'meets no wild ox or tiger')
郊: jiāo — the open ground outside the city wall — the near country where the fields lie, and so the border where armies camp
闚: kuī — to peep, look out through a chink or a window (verb; variant graph of 窺 — 不闚牖 'without peeping through the window')
陰: yīn — the shaded side of a hill, the slope turned away from the sun — hence the dark, cold, yielding aspect of things, paired with 陽 yáng
陸: lù — dry land, the ground as opposed to water (noun; 陸行 'travelling overland')
陽: yáng — the sunlit side of a hill, the slope facing the sun — hence the bright, warm, active aspect of things, paired with 陰 yīn
隅: yú — a corner, an angle (noun; the corner of a square or of a room)
隱: yǐn — to be hidden, to keep out of sight, to withdraw from view; to conceal (verb)
上士: shàng shì — the highest grade of officer — one of the three ranks of Zhou service, not simply "a superior man"
中士: zhōng shì — the middle grade of officer
下士: xià shì — the lowest grade of officer
